signals.signal: Ex-AstroBank systems migration is imminent and customer-facing: the bank tells ex-AstroBank customers the migration 'will take place in the coming period', advises them to prepare 'during August', to download Alpha 360 Mobile and activate the Alpha Secure Code service, with account access only after migration completes. Target platforms are Alpha 360 Mobile and Alpha 360 Web.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Cyprus - FAQs System Integration (Getting Started)
signals.implies: An H2-2026 cutover concentrates demand for migration testing, AML/transaction-monitoring re-tuning on the merged customer base, HSM key management for reissued cards and self-service/ATM reconfiguration - all Printec-addressable via managed services, AML/compliance and HSM/security.
signals.followup: Watch for the exact cutover weekend announcement; confirm whether card issuing/processing moves to JCC or stays on the ex-AstroBank processor

signals.entity: Central Bank of Cyprus (regulator, market context for Alpha Bank Cyprus)
signals.signal: CBC Statistical Release Payment Statistics 2nd half of 2025: total ATMs in Cyprus 396 at end-H2-2025 vs 398 at end-H2-2024; ~73% of Cyprus ATMs support contactless vs 38% in the euro area; the Cyprus ATM fleet is down ~13% over five years; average ATM withdrawal EUR 390 in H2-2025 vs EUR 307 in H2-2022 (+27%); ~EUR 2.6bn withdrawn at ATMs in H2-2025; over-the-counter cash withdrawals have almost halved in three years. Footnote 11 states that following the two systemic acquisitions completed in 2025 'further changes in the total number of ATMs in Cyprus may be observed within the coming months as the institutions reassess and rationalise their ATM networks following the integration process'.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Statistical Release, Payment Statistics: 2nd half of 2025
signals.implies: The regulator itself forecasts post-merger ATM rationalisation at Alpha Bank Cyprus and Eurobank Cyprus. Fewer but harder-working ATMs, rising withdrawal values and collapsing counter cash is precisely the case for recycler/TCR replacement plus availability-driven managed services and cash forecasting/optimisation. Also resolves the previously corrupt CBC H2-2025 PDF noted as a known gap.
signals.likelihood: High - regulator expects rationalisation within months
signals.followup: Track the CBC H1-2026 release for the post-integration ATM count; take Alpha Bank Cyprus a consolidate-and-upgrade proposal (fewer sites, recycler-class devices)

signals.signal: FY2025 audited group financial statements: 23 physical branches at 31/12/2025 (2024: 12) after incorporating the AstroBank branches; average employees 491 in 2025 (2024: 389) with 317 AstroBank staff transferred on completion 31/10/2025; computer-software additions of only EUR 4.031m in 2025 (2024: EUR 3.637m), software net book value EUR 7.270m; depreciation EUR 6.0m (2024: EUR 5.0m) increased 'due to software capitalization as part of the Bank's Digital Transformation programme'; acquired AstroBank property, plant and equipment recognised at a provisional fair value of just EUR 1.688m; acquisition fair values and negative goodwill to be finalised during 2026.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd - Group Financial Statements as at 31.12.2025 (audited by Deloitte)
signals.implies: An acquired hardware estate carried at EUR 1.7m means the ex-AstroBank ATM and branch device fleet is effectively fully depreciated and due for replacement. Software spend of ~EUR 4m a year means the bank buys packaged/managed capability rather than building - favouring Printec managed services, opex/as-a-service ATM models and cash automation over capex-heavy projects.
signals.followup: Request the ex-AstroBank ATM make/model list and remaining useful life; propose an as-a-service fleet refresh

signals.signal: The FY2025 management report sets six strategic pillars, three of them infrastructure-relevant: completion of the operational integration of AstroBank to improve customer experience, efficiency and cost synergies and cut cost-to-income; 'Upgrade of systems, processes, skills, and capabilities within the Bank to effectively support the overall Digital Transformation program'; and strong Retail growth through implementation of a 'Branch Network Redesign Program', strengthening of digital sales and service channels and deployment of CRM.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd - Group Financial Statements as at 31.12.2025, Management Report (Strategic Plan)
signals.implies: A named Branch Network Redesign Program is an open buying window for in-branch recyclers/TCRs, self-service zones and assisted-service kiosks, with a parallel systems-upgrade pillar that covers AML/monitoring and security.
signals.followup: Obtain the Branch Network Redesign Program scope and target branch count; owner is the COO / Chief Retail Banking Officer Popi Hadjioannou Demetriou

signals.signal: Voluntary Exit and Retirement Scheme announced with maximum compensation of EUR 225,000 per employee (EUR 200,000 tax-free, the excess taxed at 20%), plus an additional 10% for staff based outside Nicosia and Limassol or transferred in from doValue. Stated purpose: support the future structure of the Bank, strengthen operational flexibility and support investment in modern capabilities, skills and roles; operating-model upgrade across process streamlining and customer focus, digital transformation, and a new career framework, with role redesign and digital-skills upgrading for remaining staff.
signals.implies: This is a Cyprus-specific VES, distinct from the Greek VSS. Headcount leaving a ~746-staff bank must be replaced by automation: teller work to cash recyclers/TCRs and self-service, back-office to managed services.
signals.followup: Get the accepted headcount and cost from Alpha Services and Holdings H1/9M-2026 disclosure; pitch teller automation as the VES backfill

signals.signal: Whole-portfolio card reissue is underway for the merger: ex-AstroBank cards are replaced by new Alpha Bank cards delivered BEFORE the migration, usable only after it, with the existing card deactivated at migration; because the new cards carry new card numbers, recurring payments and subscriptions do not transfer automatically and must be re-registered by customers.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Cyprus - FAQs System Integration (Cards)
signals.implies: A full reissue with new number ranges forces rework of card personalisation, HSM/key ceremonies, ATM and POS parameter files, and 3-D Secure re-enrolment - Printec HSM/security, POS estate parameterisation and managed services.
signals.followup: Identify the personalisation bureau and the issuing processor used for the reissue

signals.signal: Branch network reorganisation is actively consolidating overlapping Alpha and ex-AstroBank sites: from 28/02/2026 the Makedonitissa branch (Engomi, Nicosia) moved into the Engomi branch (ex-AstroBank) and the Agios Ioannis branch (ex-AstroBank, Limassol) moved into the Omonias branch. A further 'Reorganization of Branch Network' corporate announcement is dated 18/03/2026.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Cyprus - Announcement, Reorganization of Branch Network (Nicosia, 12 February 2026)
signals.implies: Every merged site frees devices and raises throughput at the surviving branch, creating demand for higher-capacity recyclers and self-service zones plus ATM relocation and decommissioning work - Printec deployment and managed services.
signals.followup: Retrieve the 18/03/2026 announcement text and build a branch-by-branch overlap map to time the device proposals

signals.signal: Revision of the Bank's General Terms and Conditions (11th edition) announced 21/07/2026, effective at the earliest two months later (i.e. from late September 2026). Changes include removing references to 'ACTC' (Automated Cash Transaction Centres) from the automated-transaction-network definitions, introducing Push Notifications as a PIN delivery method, enhanced security provisions and password management for digital channels, and transitional provisions for ex-AstroBank Miles & More credit cards still active at the effective date.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Cyprus - Announcement, Revision of the General Terms and Conditions
signals.implies: The two-month notice period puts the legal effective date in late Q3-2026, consistent with a Q3/Q4-2026 systems cutover. Dropping the ACTC channel and moving PIN delivery to push notifications are self-service-estate and HSM/key-management changes - digital PIN issuance is a direct Printec HSM/security topic, and the retirement of a cash-transaction-centre channel signals estate rationalisation.
signals.likelihood: High - announced with a fixed notice period
signals.followup: Compare the 10th and 11th edition T&C texts to see exactly which self-service channels and card products are being retired

signals.signal: The bank's own Alpha 360 ATM page lists cash withdrawal, account transfers, balance and statements, credit-card payment by transfer/cash/cheque, cash deposits, cheque deposits and PIN change, available 24/7 at all Alpha Bank branch locations on 'upgraded ATMs' with 3DES encryption. Contactless/tap, cardless wallet withdrawal and voice guidance are NOT advertised on the Cyprus site, whereas Alpha Bank in Greece is introducing contactless ATM transactions under its 2026 retail banking model.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Cyprus - Alpha 360 ATM (primary) and Cyprus Mail on the Alpha retail model (02/04/2026)
signals.implies: With ~73% of Cypriot ATMs already contactless, an Alpha Cyprus fleet with no advertised NFC/cardless capability is behind both the local market and its own parent. That is a cheap, concrete upgrade sale (NFC readers plus firmware) and a lever into recycler-class replacement; the 3DES-era language also hints at an ageing key-management stack (HSM/TR-31).
signals.likelihood: Medium - inference from absence of published capability
signals.followup: Verify NFC capability model-by-model with the bank; check whether the Greek contactless-ATM rollout is being extended to Cyprus

signals.signal: Reported alongside the VES: a voluntary exit plan sized at about 80 employees, plus about 50 employees seconded to credit-acquisition company Cerberus.
signals.source_name: Eurofound restructuring events database, factsheet 107566 (Alpha Bank Cyprus, internal restructuring)
signals.implies: An ~80-head reduction on ~746 FTE (roughly 11%) plus 50 secondments means branch and back-office capacity has to be recovered through self-service, cash automation and outsourced operations.
signals.likelihood: Medium - sizing not yet confirmed on a primary source
signals.followup: Confirm the 80/50 figures with the bank or the ETYK union; open the Eurofound factsheet directly rather than via search summary

signals.signal: Salesforce Financial Services Cloud CRM fully operational since 30/04/2026, deployed in its first phase across the branch network and call centres. CEO Miltos Michaelas calls it a 'strategic investment in our digital and organisational transformation'; Salesforce RVP Kateryna Skrypchenko frames it as a 'data-driven and AI-ready foundation'; Chief Retail Banking Officer Popi Hadjioannou Demetriou is the retail sponsor.
signals.implies: CRM is now the front end of record, so the next spend layers are the servicing rails behind it: digital onboarding/eKYC feeding Salesforce, branch self-service and cash automation, and AML/monitoring on the merged base. Printec should integrate to Salesforce rather than compete with it.
signals.followup: Identify the systems integrator behind the FSC build and position eKYC/onboarding as the phase-2 add-on

signals.entity: JCC Payment Systems Ltd (Alpha Bank Cyprus is a shareholder bank)
signals.signal: Card acquiring, clearing and settlement in Cyprus runs through JCC Cards Payment System, owned and operated by JCC Payment Systems Ltd, which processes authorisations from issuing banks and clears/settles Visa, Mastercard and Diners transactions for the participating banks. The CBC also notes card acquiring is provided in Cyprus mainly by payment/e-money institutions rather than analysed separately in its statistics.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Retail Payment Systems
signals.implies: Bank-level POS/acquiring at Alpha Bank Cyprus is structurally routed through the bank-owned JCC utility, so Printec's POS route into this account is via JCC and merchant estate services rather than a direct bank acquiring sale; Printec Cyprus already services a large POS base locally.
signals.followup: Map Printec Cyprus's existing JCC/merchant relationships and check whether the ex-AstroBank merchant estate is being re-terminalised during the migration

coverage_notes: Fresh run, no checkpoint existed. Angles used this run: (1) the bank's own ex-AstroBank migration microsite and its per-topic FAQ subpages (getting-started, cards) - these are the freshest primary source and gave the August-preparation instruction and the full card reissue; (2) the audited FY2025 Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd group financial statements PDF, downloaded with a desktop UA and text-extracted locally, giving branch count, headcount, software additions and the acquired PP&E fair value plus the six strategic pillars including the Branch Network Redesign Program; (3) the bank's corporate announcements list and the branch-reorganisation and General T&C announcements; (4) the Central Bank of Cyprus publications index and the H2-2025 Payment Statistics release (the exact file the previous run found corrupt - now retrieved and parsed, resolving that known gap); (5) Greek-language Cypriot press (Politis) for the Voluntary Exit Scheme; (6) the CBC retail payment systems page for the JCC acquiring structure. Genuine gaps: the ATM/self-service OEM at Alpha Bank Cyprus and at ex-AstroBank remains unidentified despite direct searching (standing task); the post-integration ATM count is unresolved (press cites 26 branches/31 ATMs post-deal, the CBN member-bank table cites 25/26 at the start of 2026, the audited statements say 23 branches at 31/12/2025, and the CBC only publishes the island total of 396); the 18/03/2026 branch reorganisation announcement text could not be retrieved (PDF link not exposed in the server-rendered HTML); Alpha Services and Holdings H1-2026 results were not yet published at the run date, so no 2026 Cyprus segment figures. The Cyprus Mail 02/04/2026 'retail banking transformation plan' article is about Alpha Bank in GREECE (Psaltis, five directorates and 25 regions, contactless ATMs) and has deliberately NOT been attributed to Cyprus.
access_issues: centralbank.cy returns HTTP 403 to the fetch tool and silently serves its homepage for guessed PDF paths; resolved by curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent plus the real publications index at /en/publications/payment-statistics, then local pdfminer extraction. The Alpha Bank Cyprus press-office listing is JS-rendered, so announcement PDFs had to be located via search; one curl of that path returned unrelated cached markup. Alpha Bank Cyprus PDFs (branch reorganisation, FY2025 statements) are not readable by the fetch tool and were extracted locally with pdfminer. The /en/astrobank/faqs-migration path 404s; the working path is /en/astrobank/customer-information/faqs-migration. No source was dropped silently.
